question: Sapna invested ₹20,400 on simple interest, partly at the rate of 14% per annum and partly at the rate of 11% per annum. If she earns equal interests from the two investments after 9 years, then find the sum invested at the rate of 14% per annum (in ₹).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When Simple Interests from two investments are equal for the same time period, their principals are inversely proportional to their rates.

Ratio of Principals P₁ : P₂ = R₂ : R₁ = 11 : 14

Total ratio parts = 11 + 14 = 25 parts.

Value of 25 parts = ₹20,400 ⇒ 1 part = ₹816.

Sum invested at 14% (11 parts) = 11 × 816 = 8976.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹8,976.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Principal = ₹20,400

Rate 1 (R₁) = 14% p.a., Time 1 (T₁) = 9 years

Rate 2 (R₂) = 11% p.a., Time 2 (T₂) = 9 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100
